title: Kilnmore ceramics paid-social kit: neutralise an 8-SKU two-session product batch to one white point against an in-frame grey card, bring the signature glazes to house colour, knock each onto pure white, and merge one typeset ad card per SKU
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork 'Graphic designer - advertising creatives' open call (a DTC brand wanting 'high-performing static ad creatives, promotional graphics, and multiple creative variations for testing across our paid social campaigns,' working 'from existing brand guidelines,' with 'clean, modern, conversion-focused visuals' for an e-commerce homeware brand, ongoing collaboration). The real post names no client and attaches no images, so the brand is laundered to a FICTIONAL matte-ceramic homeware label, 'Kilnmore', and no real social platform, network, ad product, or trademark is named anywhere (the destinations are described generically as the square feed, portrait feed, and vertical full-screen formats; only the sourcing site, Upwork, is named, in source.platform). REPOSITIONED for connector reality and to fix the prior version's two defects: (1) the earlier spec ran ONE hero and 'handed off the typeset final assembly to a human' — the paid work the client actually commissioned. This version restores a real product-line BATCH (eight SKUs shot across two sessions under deliberately mismatched light, each with a photographic 18% grey card in frame) and ends in an AGENT-OWNED designed artifact: the ad copy is actually set in type through a genuine hand-authored InDesign data-merge, not punted. (2) The earlier prose instructed banned AI outpaint for the ratio canvases; here every frame is an honest crop of existing pixels, no canvas added. The client supplies eight raw product photos, a flat wordmark scan, a hand-authored single-record InDesign ad-card template (.indd, NOT a converted PDF) carrying live <<fields>> plus TWO @-prefixed image-path columns, and the ad roster as a CSV. House accent glaze colour is pinned (brand teal #1E6E66) and the sage serving glaze is a second signature colour, so 'on-brand colour' becomes a measurable target rather than an eyeball claim. No generative fill/expand, no compositing, no text-to-image, no upscaling, no free-form placement is claimed.
one_line_ask: Take eight Kilnmore product photos shot across two mismatched-light sessions (each with a grey card in frame), neutralise every frame to its card so the line reads as one white point, bring the signature glazes to their true house colours without letting saturated pieces glow or near-neutral pieces pick up a tint, knock each product cleanly onto pure white with its soft edges intact, cut the hero to the three platform ratios, vectorise the wordmark, then data-merge the client's authored ad-card template so one finished, typeset paid-social ad ships per SKU.
full_brief:
Kilnmore is a DTC matte-ceramic homeware label about to run paid-social tests across the square feed, the portrait feed, and the vertical full-screen format, and we need the imagery-plus-ad layer built to our brand guidelines. Here is the honest situation: our catalogue was shot over two afternoons in whatever corner of the studio was free, so the raw set does not match. About half the pieces were shot by a cool north window and half under our warm work-lamps, a couple came in a little tilted, one or two under- or over-exposed. Because we knew the light was inconsistent, we clipped a neutral 18% grey balance card into the corner of every single frame.

What we need back, and the bar we will judge against:

1) Make the whole product line read as ONE deliberately-designed set, not eight mismatched snapshots. Use the grey card in each frame as ground truth: every image must be neutralised so its card reads truly neutral (no residual warm, cool or green cast) and so the cards sit at one common brightness across the set, tolerance about three levels of channel spread on each card and the set's mid-grey within roughly four levels of a common target. Do NOT force one blanket correction across the batch — each frame was lit differently and needs its own white-balance and exposure decision to land on the shared target. When you are done, tell us, per image, the white-balance and exposure move you settled on, so we can confirm the set was matched to the card and not just eyeballed.

2) Carry ONE restrained, premium house look across all eight — a slightly warm-highlight, clean-neutral-shadow ceramic tone with modest contrast, a little clarity and a gentle vibrance lift, so the finish reads warm and expensive head to head. But hold our two signature glazes to their true brand values: our accent teal is exactly #1E6E66 and the sage serving pieces are our second brand colour, and these must read the same true colour whichever session they were shot in — the teal rich and green, never muddy or gone-cyan. The catch our last freelancer missed: keep genuinely saturated pieces from glowing hot under the vibrance push, and keep near-neutral pieces (our sand and oatmeal bodies) from picking up any tint. Colour truth is per-piece judgement, not one global slider, and a piece whose glaze is already true must be left alone rather than 'corrected' toward an imagined cast.

3) Put every product on a catalogue-clean pure-white background (#FFFFFF) with the studio sweep and the grey card gone, isolated with a clean, natural edge — handles, spouts and rims soft and real, no hard cardboard-cutout halo and nothing bricked in with a flat plate where the piece opens up. 

4) The signature pour-over dripper is our hero: give us that piece, on white and on-look, cut to the three platform ratios (1:1 square, 4:5 portrait, 9:16 vertical) by honestly reframing the existing shot to each ratio, product centred, no canvas invented.

5) Turn our wordmark, which only exists as a slightly skewed scan on off-white stock, into razor-sharp vector art for crisp use at any ad size.

6) Finally, SET THE ADS. We are giving you our authored InDesign ad-card template and the ad roster: merge them so every SKU gets its own finished single-page ad with its matched packshot placed, our crisp wordmark placed, and its headline, offer, price and call-to-action set in type from the roster. Bind the copy verbatim from the roster; do not rewrite it. Hand back one press-ready PDF, one typeset ad per SKU (the hero simply first).

Deliver: the eight matched white-background packshots, the hero's three-ratio set, the vector wordmark, the merged per-SKU ad PDF, and the per-image parameter note.

inputs.name: kilnmore_dripper_teal_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A real full-frame DSLR/mirrorless camera capture, ~4200 px on the long edge, of a single matte-ceramic pour-over coffee dripper in a soft teal-green glaze, standing on a near-white seamless paper sweep, its open cone and small looped handle clearly visible. A photographic 18% neutral grey card with a small white patch lies flat on the sweep at the lower-left edge of frame. Shot under WARM tungsten work-lamp light with a distinct orange cast, slightly flat and marginally under-exposed, and the whole frame tilted about 3 degrees off level. Real ceramic micro-texture, faint glaze speckle, a soft contact shadow. Straight off the camera, un-graded, documentary product realism, no props, no text, not CGI-glossy.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU-01, HERO and the multi-ratio piece. Session B (warm/orange), tilted ~3 deg and slightly under so its corrective white-balance/exposure differs from every other frame. Its teal glaze is the brand accent and MUST end matched to the cool-session teal mug (SKU-02) at the house teal #1E6E66 — the two teals are shot under OPPOSITE casts, so a single shared white balance cannot neutralise both and copying one glaze correction onto the other is the cross-session-match trap. The looped handle and open cone give the knockout genuine soft interior edges: because the delivered ground is white and the sweep is near-white, the enclosed openings simply read clean white; the failure is a flat select->invert->fill plate that bricks them with a hard halo. Grey card is the neutralisation ground truth; it is cropped OUT of the delivered packshot, so neutrality is graded on the retained neutralised master.

inputs.name: kilnmore_mug_teal_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A real full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a single matte-ceramic stacking mug in the same teal-green glaze as the dripper, on a near-white seamless paper sweep, its C-shaped handle open to the background. A photographic 18% grey card with a white patch sits on the sweep at the lower-right edge of frame. Shot under COOL north-window daylight with a clear blue cast, roughly normal exposure. Real matte-ceramic texture, natural soft contact shadow, un-graded documentary product shot, no text, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU-02. Session A (cool/blue): the OPPOSITE corrective direction to the warm dripper, so a single blanket white balance across the batch cannot neutralise both cards — this is the uniform-WB trap. Same brand teal glaze as SKU-01; the two must converge on ONE house teal #1E6E66 despite starting from opposite casts, so its masked glaze correction is close-but-not-equal to the dripper's and cannot be copied. Card is the target.

inputs.name: kilnmore_creamer_rust_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A real full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a small matte-ceramic milk creamer in a saturated rust/terracotta glaze, on a near-white seamless paper sweep, its handle and pour spout visible. A photographic 18% grey card with a white patch sits on the sweep at the frame edge. Shot under WARM tungsten work-lamp light with an orange cast that pushes the already-saturated rust glaze near-glowing with the highlights on the shoulder just short of clipping. Real ceramic sheen and glaze pooling, soft contact shadow, un-graded documentary product shot, no text, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU-03. Session B (warm). OVER-CORRECTION trap: neutralising the orange cast and then adding the shared vibrance lift drives the rust radioactive and clips it. Its masked glaze pass must RESTRAIN — pull saturation and drop the luminance of the hottest shoulder toward the true house rust — the OPPOSITE move to the teal pieces, so the agent must compute per-hue direction, not a blanket 'make colours pop'. Card is the target.

inputs.name: kilnmore_sugar_canister_sand_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A real full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a matte-ceramic lidded sugar canister in a pale sand / warm-greige glaze, on a near-white seamless paper sweep, small knob handle on the lid. A photographic 18% grey card with a white patch sits on the sweep at the frame edge. Shot under WARM tungsten work-lamp light with an orange cast, slightly bright. Real matte texture and soft folds of shadow, un-graded documentary product shot, no text, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU-04. Session B (warm). Triage partner to SKU-05: a near-neutral pale body that superficially resembles the oatmeal bowls but was shot under the OPPOSITE session, so it needs a cool-ward correction where SKU-05 needs a warm-ward one. Applying one near-neutral recipe to both is the triage trap — the wrong route leaves a residual cast that is invisible until inspected. Restraint case: over-correcting tints the sand fabric; a correct grey-card neutralisation leaves the sand believable.

inputs.name: kilnmore_nesting_bowls_oatmeal_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A real full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a nested pair of matte-ceramic prep bowls in a warm oatmeal glaze, on a near-white seamless paper sweep, a clear gap between the two bowl rims. A photographic 18% grey card with a white patch sits on the sweep at the lower edge of frame, and the whole frame is tilted about 4 degrees off level. Shot under COOL north-window daylight with a blue cast, flat contrast. Real matte-ceramic texture, faint contact shadow, un-graded documentary product shot, no text, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU-05. Session A (cool), tilted ~4 deg. Triage partner to SKU-04: near-neutral oatmeal that looks like the sand canister but was shot COOL, so its correct move is opposite; treating the two the same fails. Two-object frame, so the semantic isolation spans both bowls. Restraint case — don't drive the warm oatmeal grey chasing the blue cast. Card is the target.

inputs.name: kilnmore_espresso_cup_charcoal_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A real full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a matte-ceramic espresso cup and saucer in a deep charcoal glaze, on a near-white seamless paper sweep, cup handle open to the background. A photographic 18% grey card with a white patch sits on the sweep at the frame edge. Shot under COOL north-window daylight with a blue cast and clearly UNDER-exposed, so the dark charcoal muddies toward black. Real matte nap and soft folds, faint contact shadow, un-graded documentary product shot, no text, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU-06. Session A (cool), under-exposed. Black-point discipline: warm to the card and LIFT exposure to the set brightness while holding the black point so the charcoal stays charcoal, not crushed to pure zero and not washed to grey. Its dark edge against the white sweep isolates easily — contrast with the near-white crock (SKU-08). Card is the target.

inputs.name: kilnmore_serving_platter_sage_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A real full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a matte-ceramic oval serving platter in a genuine soft sage-green glaze (the brand's second signature colour), on a near-white seamless paper sweep. A photographic 18% grey card with a white patch sits on the sweep at the frame edge. Shot under WARM tungsten work-lamp light that is gentle enough here that the card reads close to neutral straight out of camera, roughly normal exposure. Real matte-glaze texture and soft rim shadow, un-graded documentary product shot, no text, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU-07. Session B, but lit gently so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads close to neutral. HOLD-WB trap: the sage glaze is a genuine brand colour, not a cast, so the correct move is essentially no white-balance shift (only match brightness to the set). A naive agent that batch-applies the same 'cool the warm session' correction used on the other warm frames, or 'corrects an imagined cast', pushes its card off-neutral and strips the real sage the client is selling. Decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch.

inputs.name: kilnmore_utensil_crock_ecru_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A real full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a matte-ceramic utensil crock in an ecru / off-white glaze, empty, on a near-white seamless paper sweep, so the pale crock sits at very low contrast against the pale sweep. A photographic 18% grey card with a white patch sits on the sweep at the frame edge. Shot under COOL north-window daylight with a faint blue cast, gentle exposure. Real subtle matte texture and a very soft contact shadow, un-graded documentary product shot, no text, low fabric-to-background contrast, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU-08. Session A (cool). Hardest isolation edge in the batch: a near-white ecru body on a near-white sweep, so a clean knockout demands prompt-anchored semantic subject isolation, not a luminance guess. Also a WB restraint case — neutralise the faint cast without driving the ecru grey. Card is the target.

inputs.name: kilnmore_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'KILNMORE' wordmark inked on off-white textured paper: a confident geometric sans-serif in deep charcoal, with a small simple dripper-cone line glyph to the left of the word. Rendered as a real scan — the paper is a slightly warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 deg) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around it, and the edges are a touch soft as a real scan would be. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will vectorize cleanly.
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, ~2 deg rotation, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize would trace the paper and the skew if fed raw — forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, crisp the contrast, crop to the mark, knock the off-white ground to transparency, THEN vectorize. gemini-3-pro-image chosen for clean legible lettering. Reaches every ad card as a merge bind through the template's second @-image column, never by free-form placement.

inputs.name: kilnmore_adcard_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD portrait paid-social ad card (4:5, built at 1080x1350 px scale) — ONE ad per page. It carries live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<headline>>, <<offer>>, <<price>>, <<cta>>, and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a product image frame bound to @packshot (the matching matched white-background packshot) and a logo frame bound to @wordmark (the vectorised Kilnmore wordmark). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, both images reach the layout ONLY as merge binds through these two image frames. Built by hand in InDesign so the text fields and BOTH image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout requires a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it emits ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record ad card is the correct, connector-doable shape (a converted-PDF template or a multi-up grid would not bind / cannot be produced). TWO image columns (@packshot, @wordmark) mean the merge resolves two prepped assets per row — the row's matched packshot AND the shared vectorised wordmark — giving the chain-produced wordmark a real path onto every ad without any free-form placement (mirrors the two-image-column pattern in the passing bakery and apparel exemplars). Supplied as an input, not a chain output.

inputs.name: kilnmore_ad_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED asset (client-supplied): an 8-row data-merge CSV, one row per SKU, with text columns headline, offer, price, cta and TWO @-prefixed image-path columns, @packshot and @wordmark. @packshot names that SKU's matched white-background packshot file the agent produces; @wordmark holds the SAME vectorised wordmark file (kilnmore_wordmark.svg) in every row. Header names match the template's <<headline>>, <<offer>>, <<price>>, <<cta>> fields and its two @-image columns exactly. Row 1 is the hero pour-over dripper. Copy is final client marketing copy, bound verbatim.
inputs.realism_notes: The @packshot column is the binding contract: the agent must point each cell at its own produced packshot so the merge places each matched product onto its ad; @wordmark carries the identical wordmark SVG in all eight rows so the shared mark lands on every ad as a merge bind. Row count = 8 fixes the page=row acceptance gate. document_merge_data_vector is the WRONG tool (text-only, cannot bind either image column). Columns state ad content only; no per-frame diagnosis or treatment is encoded in the data.

outputs.name: matched_packshots_x8
outputs.spec: Eight product packshots (SKU-01..SKU-08), each neutralised to its in-frame 18% grey card and matched to ONE shared white point and brightness across the whole line, carrying the single restrained house look, with the two signature glazes held to their true house values (accent teal #1E6E66 on both teal pieces; sage genuine) and near-neutral bodies left believable, then each product isolated onto a pure solid-white (#FFFFFF) background with the sweep and grey card gone, soft natural edges on handles/spouts/rims, no hard cardboard-cutout halo and no flat plate bricking the openings. sRGB, long edge 2048 px. Acceptance (grader-checked, TWO SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralisation and white-point match are graded on the RETAINED pre-knockout neutralised master of each frame (the *_neutralised full-res output, grey card still in frame) — each card reads neutral (per-channel spread within ~3 levels) with the set's mid-grey within ~4 levels of a common target, true-to-glaze (no piece's genuine colour forced off, no near-neutral body tinted); (b) card-exclusion is checked SEPARATELY on each delivered white-background packshot (grey card fully cropped out / removed with the background). The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the delivered packshot. Accompanied by the per-image parameter report.

outputs.name: hero_ratio_set
outputs.spec: The hero pour-over dripper (SKU-01), matched, on-look and on pure white, delivered at the three platform ratios by HONEST reframing of the existing graded packshot: 1:1 square (1080x1080), 4:5 portrait (1080x1350), and 9:16 vertical (1080x1920), product centred, the near-white margins trimming to hit each ratio. No canvas is added, padded, or extended and no pixels are generated; each is a single downscale/reframe of existing pixels (source is camera-scale, so every crop is downscale-only).

outputs.name: kilnmore_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the KILNMORE wordmark + dripper glyph, traced only AFTER the scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark, and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at any ad size with no captured paper ground and no skew. Also the mark bound into every ad card's logo frame via the roster's @wordmark column.

outputs.name: kilnmore_adcards_perSKU.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly eight press-ready portrait paid-social ad cards — ONE typeset ad per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each ad binds its headline/offer/price/cta verbatim from the roster, drops that SKU's matched white-background packshot into the product frame (via @packshot) and the vectorised wordmark into the logo frame (via @wordmark), both by merge bind, never free-form placement. The hero dripper is simply page 1. This is the finished, TYPESET ad deliverable the client commissioned — the type is actually set here, not handed off. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged document in one call, so there is no per-record named export; the hero is page 1 of this PDF.

outputs.name: grade_params_report
outputs.spec: A short accompanying note (secondary to the images, NOT the primary deliverable) in which the agent reports, per image: the corrective white-balance move it settled on to hit the card (temperature and tint direction/magnitude), the exposure delta, and — for the colour-critical pieces — the masked glaze move applied, plus a one-line confirmation that each frame's grey card reads neutral and lands on the common target. This makes 'matched to the card' verifiable rather than asserted. It is a report of parameters the agent CHOSE and applied, never a measured pixel/hex readout.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: kilnmore_dripper_teal_raw.jpg, kilnmore_mug_teal_raw.jpg, kilnmore_creamer_rust_raw.jpg, kilnmore_sugar_canister_sand_raw.jpg, kilnmore_nesting_bowls_oatmeal_raw.jpg, kilnmore_espresso_cup_charcoal_raw.jpg, kilnmore_serving_platter_sage_raw.jpg, kilnmore_utensil_crock_ecru_raw.jpg, kilnmore_wordmark_scan.png, kilnmore_adcard_template.indd, kilnmore_ad_roster.csv
connector_workflow.note: Load the eight product photos, the wordmark scan, the authored ad-card .indd template and the ad roster CSV into the working project in one batch so every downstream step runs against real asset references. Single upload — plumbing, not counted as difficulty.
SKU-01 (hero): level this frame before any grade or reframe, since it came in off level; deciding which frames need levelling is part of the job.

SKU-01: neutralise this frame to its in-frame 18% grey card so it lands on the shared set white point, reasoning THIS frame's own white-balance and exposure from its card rather than a batch constant, and lay in the shared house-look constants (warm-highlight / neutral-shadow split-tone, modest contrast, a little clarity, gentle vibrance). Authored from primitives, not a preset and not auto-tone. Retain this card-bearing neutralised master — neutrality is graded here, not on the later cropped packshot. Report the white-balance/exposure values chosen.

Semantically select only the glazed ceramic body of this piece ('the teal glazed ceramic dripper') so the colour-truth move is confined to the glaze and never touches the grey card, white patch or sweep. Returns a maskURI; a named object, not a hue or coordinate region.

Masked colour-truth pass (consumes the neutralised frame + glaze mask): bring this piece's glaze to the house accent target #1E6E66, holding the ceramic's own luminosity so the matte finish stays real. image_adjust_hsl is the only masked-recolour path; image_apply_color_overlay (whole-image) and image_fill_area (flat dead-fill) are both wrong here. A bounded in-family adjustment, no near-complementary rotation.

Knock this product onto a solid pure-white PDP ground via image_remove_background with backgroundColor #FFFFFF. This is the connector-legal knockout: it isolates the product as foreground with a soft natural edge and removes the sweep AND the grey card. Deliberately NOT the select_subject -> invert_selection -> image_fill_area plate chain, which hard-halos the edge and bricks the handle/cone openings with a flat fill.

Resize the hero knockout to the shared packshot spec (long edge 2048 px, sRGB), product centred. Downscale/reframe only, onSubjectClipping='extract', never canvas-extend, never upscale. Feeds both the matched-packshots deliverable and this SKU's @packshot merge cell.
Honest 1:1 reframe of the hero knockout to 1080x1080, product centred, near-white margins trimming to the square. Crop of existing pixels only; no canvas added, no generation.
Honest 4:5 reframe of the hero knockout to 1080x1350, product centred. Crop of existing pixels only; no canvas added, no generation.

Honest 9:16 reframe of the hero knockout to 1080x1920, product centred, the wider margins trimming to the tall vertical. Crop of existing pixels only; no canvas added, no generation. hero_1x1/hero_4x5/hero_9x16 form hero_ratio_set.

SKU-02: neutralise to its own in-frame grey card to the shared white point, reasoning this frame's white-balance/exposure from its card (its correction is not the hero's — the light differed), and lay in the same shared house-look constants. Retain this card-bearing neutralised master for grading. Report the values chosen.
Semantically select this piece's glazed ceramic body only so its colour-truth move stays off the card and sweep. Returns a maskURI.

Masked colour-truth pass: bring this piece's glaze to the SAME house accent target #1E6E66 the hero was matched to, so the two signature pieces read identical house colour despite starting from different casts. Cross-asset colour match to a common target on the only masked-recolour path; luminosity preserved, bounded in-family shift.
Knock SKU-02 onto solid white via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); soft handle edge preserved, no flat-fill plate. Same anti-pattern avoidance as step 6.
Resize to the shared packshot spec (2048 px long edge, sRGB), product centred. Downscale/reframe only. Feeds SKU-02's @packshot cell.

SKU-03: neutralise to its in-frame grey card to the shared white point, reasoning this frame's own white-balance/exposure, holding the highlights so the saturated glaze does not clip before the colour-truth pass; lay in the shared house-look constants. Retain the card-bearing master. Report the values.
Semantically select this piece's glazed ceramic body only. Returns a maskURI.

Masked colour-truth pass: settle this piece's glaze onto its true house value by pulling saturation and dropping the luminance of the hottest area so the finish reads rich, not glowing or clipped — the opposite direction to the teal pieces' pass. Riding the original luminosity so the matte sheen stays natural; the only masked-recolour path, no whole-image overlay, no flat fill.
Knock SKU-03 onto solid white via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); soft spout/handle edges preserved.
Resize to the shared packshot spec, product centred. Downscale/reframe only. Feeds SKU-03's @packshot cell.

SKU-04: neutralise to its in-frame grey card to the shared white point, reasoning this frame's own white-balance/exposure and holding the near-neutral body believable rather than tinting it; lay in the shared house-look constants. This piece needs a genuinely different correction from the similar-looking near-neutral piece elsewhere in the batch. Retain the card-bearing master. Report the values.

Knock SKU-04 onto solid white via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); no masked colour pass needed (glaze is not a signature accent), so it isolates straight from the neutralised frame.
Resize to the shared packshot spec, product centred. Downscale/reframe only. Feeds SKU-04's @packshot cell.
SKU-05: level this frame, which came in off level, before grading.

SKU-05: neutralise to its in-frame grey card to the shared white point, reasoning this frame's own white-balance/exposure (its move is opposite to the similar-looking near-neutral piece shot in the other session) and holding the near-neutral body believable; lay in the shared house-look constants. Retain the card-bearing master. Report the values.
Knock SKU-05 onto solid white via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); the semantic isolation spans both nested bowls, and the rim gap simply reads clean white on the white ground.
Resize to the shared packshot spec, subjects centred. Downscale/reframe only. Feeds SKU-05's @packshot cell.

SKU-06: neutralise to its in-frame grey card to the shared white point, reasoning this frame's own white-balance and lifting exposure to the set brightness while holding the black point so the dark glaze stays deep but is not crushed to zero or washed to grey; lay in the shared house-look constants. Retain the card-bearing master. Report the values.
Knock SKU-06 onto solid white via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); the dark glaze cuts cleanly against white — contrast with the low-contrast near-white piece.
Resize to the shared packshot spec, product centred. Downscale/reframe only. Feeds SKU-06's @packshot cell.

SKU-07: neutralise to its in-frame grey card to the shared white point — this frame's card is already close to neutral, so the correct move is essentially to hold white balance and only match brightness to the set, NOT to push a correction that would strip the genuine signature glaze; lay in the shared house-look constants. Read THIS card, not the batch. Retain the card-bearing master. Report that white balance was held.
Knock SKU-07 onto solid white via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); soft rim edge preserved.
Resize to the shared packshot spec, product centred. Downscale/reframe only. Feeds SKU-07's @packshot cell.

SKU-08: neutralise to its in-frame grey card to the shared white point, reasoning this frame's own white-balance and holding the near-white body believable (not driven grey) while protecting the tonal separation the isolation step needs against the white sweep; lay in the shared house-look constants. Retain the card-bearing master. Report the values.

Prep-before-trace step 1: the wordmark scan sits slightly rotated on the bed — straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drop the off-white paper toward white so the charcoal lettering separates hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark and glyph, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill).

difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship with difficulty from DEPTH, not plumbing: 45 connector calls, 13 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (image_* grading/masking/vectorize, asset_* storage, document_* merge/export), well above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the single batch upload, the two merge-upload steps and the three auto-straighten auto-ops. The core is not a repeated recipe: each of the eight neutralisations is a DIFFERENT reasoned decision (opposite casts across two sessions, a saturated piece to restrain, near-neutral bodies to hold, an under-exposed dark piece to lift on its black point, a genuinely-coloured piece whose card is already neutral to leave alone) all forced to converge on one measurable target — each frame's in-frame 18% grey card at a shared white point — so a blanket batch correction cannot pass. Layered on top are an agent-authored house look built from image_apply_adjustments primitives (split-tone + contrast/clarity/vibrance) applied as shared constants (NOT a preset, NOT auto-tone), three masked luminosity-preserving glaze passes that move in OPPOSITE directions (match the two signature teal pieces to one house target #1E6E66; restrain the saturated rust so it stops glowing), a connector-legal knockout onto pure white via remove_background({backgroundColor}) that avoids the flat-plate select->invert->fill anti-pattern (including a low-contrast near-white-on-white isolation edge), an honest three-ratio hero reframe with no canvas invented, a genuine prep-before-trace vectorise of a skewed off-white scan, and a two-image-column one-file-per-row data-merge into a hand-authored single-record template that actually SETS the ad copy in type — the paid work the prior version punted to a human. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no compositing, no upscaling, no from-scratch layout; convert_pdf_to_indd is not used; image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract'; deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _brightness_and_contrast / _vibrance_and_saturation are replaced by image_apply_adjustments.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): every product frame carries a physical 18% grey card and the acceptance test is that each card, graded on its RETAINED pre-knockout neutralised master (grey card still in frame), reads truly neutral (per-channel spread within ~3 levels) with the set's mid-grey within ~4 levels of a common target — and the agent must REPORT the per-image white-balance/exposure move it chose, so a naive agent that copies one white balance across the two-session batch leaves the cool frames blue and the warm frames orange and trips the gate; a second knockout gate (soft natural edge, no flat-plate halo, openings not bricked) and a third merge gate (output page-count must equal roster row-count = 8) round it out. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset neutralisation of eight differently-lit product shots to one measurable white point, each needing its own, often opposite-direction correction; (2) cross-session colour match of the two signature teal pieces to one house target #1E6E66 through masked luminosity-preserving HSL — a value a novice cannot hold by eye — while restraining the saturated rust so it does not clip and holding near-neutral bodies believable; (3) triage of two superficially identical near-neutral pieces shot under OPPOSITE sessions into DIFFERENT correct treatments, where a wrong route is invisible until inspected; (4) prep-before-trace discipline on a skewed off-white wordmark scan before vectorize; (5) a near-white-on-white isolation edge. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (decoupled so no artifact is graded on a region it crops away): (a) grey card neutral (~3-level spread) and one shared white point, evaluated on all eight RETAINED pre-knockout neutralised masters (card in frame), never on a card-removed packshot; (b) card-exclusion checked separately on the eight delivered white-background packshots; the two teal pieces landing on #1E6E66, the rust not clipping, near-neutral bodies untinted; the hero at 1:1/4:5/9:16 (1080x1080 / 1080x1350 / 1080x1920) with no canvas added; the wordmark a clean skew-free transparent-ground vector; and exactly one typeset ad per roster row (page-count = 8) with the copy set in type via the merge — plus the per-image parameter report so 'matched to the card' is verifiable rather than asserted.
